assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes (unchanged)
daemon_capability: full (WAS bug at e055cef4 -- flipped by commit 609cb28d, re-verified live in this session)
driver_capability: gap:settings_model (unchanged, re-confirmed against the current file)

Route: driver-gap. This is a RE-ASSESSMENT of e055cef4, which itself superseded two earlier 'frozen, no Go adapter' verdicts once a real adapter shipped. This pass re-judges both pillars against the code as it stands rather than deferring to the prior verdict, per the assignment's explicit instruction not to preserve a stale verdict out of deference.

## agent_supports -- yes (carried forward, unaffected by either fix)

Unchanged from e055cef4: `muse --help` documents a top-level `--model <MODEL>` flag; the prior assessment live-drove `muse --trust-workspace --model muse-spark-1.2` on this machine and captured a session.jsonl carrying `run.model.configured.record.model_id`, `runtime.session.metadata.record.model_id`, and `model_completed.model` all equal to `muse-spark-1.2` (the non-default pin; the account default is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`). Neither fix commit (609cb28d, daemon; 0239a1bd, driver) touches model selection surface, so this verdict does not need re-driving to stand -- it is orthogonal to both changes. `muse --version` on this machine still reports `1.2.1-R2847.1`, matching the version this verdict was captured against.

## daemon_capability -- full (RE-JUDGED: was bug, now full)

The scenario's acceptance criteria are exactly two: `ModelName = <launch model>` (not 'unknown'), and `ContextWindow` matches the model's published window. Both are now satisfied by the code as it stands, and I independently re-ran the mechanism rather than trusting the fix commit's own claim:

**ModelName: full, unchanged.** `parseRunModelConfigured`/`parseMetadata`/`parseModelCompleted` (parser.go) all funnel into `applyModelIdentity` (parser.go:654-659), which sets `ev.ModelName = tailer.NormalizeModelName(model)` from the raw model id irrespective of the fix below.

**ContextWindow: now full.** Two independent, previously-stacked gaps are both closed:

1. `parseModelCompleted` (parser.go:371-442) now sets `ev.Tokens.Total` (line 439: `bd.Input + bd.Output + bd.CacheRead + bd.CacheCreation5m`) -- I read the current file myself; this is the exact line the prior assessment cited as omitted. `applyTokenSnapshot` (core/pkg/tailer/tailer_metrics.go) copies this into `SessionMetrics.TotalTokens` only when `.Total > 0`, so `TotalTokens` now populates for every muse session with usage, unblocking `computeContextUtilization`'s early-return guard.
2. A NEW fallback source closes the second, previously-unfixable gap: `applyModelIdentity` (parser.go:656-658) also calls `contextWindowForModel(model)` (catalog.go), which scans every `*.json` file under `~/.local/share/muse/model-catalog/` -- a cache muse's OWN binary treats as its canonical effective-context-limit fallback (cited in the fix commit via a `strings` scan of the muse binary: "effective context limit from provider_context_limit_tokens or model catalog context limit" / "using the cached catalog with the default context budget") -- for a `rows[]` entry whose `model_id` matches exactly, returning its `context_limit`. This was NOT available at the prior assessment (core/pkg/capacity's LiteLLM snapshot still has zero muse/spark entries, confirmed again below, and that gap alone would have kept ContextWindow unresolvable) -- catalog.go bypasses the pricing-catalog dependency entirely by reading muse's own local cache instead.

   **Independently re-verified, not taken from the commit message:** I wrote a throwaway `go run` probe (`tailer.NewTranscriptTailer(path, &muse.Parser{}, muse.AdapterName).TailAndProcess()`) against the committed fixture `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/testdata/real-turn-completed.jsonl` and got `TotalTokens=35401 ContextWindow=1007997 ContextWindowUnknown=false ModelName="muse-spark-1.3-contributor" CumInputTokens=35082 CumOutputTokens=477` -- matching the fix commit's own claimed before/after figures exactly, confirmed by my own run against the actual production code, not by reading the commit message. `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -race -count=1` passes (re-ran it in this session).

**Caveat -- this is a local-filesystem read, not a transcript signal, and that is a real recipe precondition (Vacuous-pass rule).** `contextWindowForModel` reads `$HOME/.local/share/muse/model-catalog/*.json` directly via `os.ReadDir`/`os.ReadFile` (catalog.go:61-68) -- a side-channel muse itself lazily populates, NOT a field inside `events.jsonl`/the session transcript. `catalog_test.go`'s `TestContextWindowForModel_NoDirectory` pins the honest degrade: an absent directory returns `(0, false)`, which `computeContextUtilization` reports as `ContextWindowUnknown=true`, not a fabricated number -- so the mechanism is honest but it depends on this cache already existing on the RECORDING machine. If `record` runs on a machine/account where muse has never resolved this model's context limit before (a fresh install, or a model the account has never actually launched), `ContextWindow` will legitimately read unknown even though the daemon mechanism is fully correct. This belongs in the recipe's preconditions, not just as an aside (see below).

**Caveat -- the SPECIFIC pinned model's catalog row is unconfirmed.** The only catalog rows anyone has directly observed on this machine are `muse-spark-1.3` and `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (catalog.go's doc comment cites one real file with an entry for the session's default model; `catalog_test.go`'s `TestContextWindowForModel_MatchFound` fixture separately includes a `muse-spark-1.3` row -- both traceable to the same original live observation, not two independent confirmations). The recipe pins `muse-spark-1.2` (the non-default model), and whether THAT model has its own row in the live catalog file is inferred, not confirmed -- plausible since the picker enumerates it as a selectable option (so muse likely already resolved its context limit once), but `record` must verify `ContextWindow > 0` actually resolves for `muse-spark-1.2` specifically when it runs, not merely that the mechanism exists in the abstract.

**cost_nonzero: false, unaffected, independently reconfirmed.** `core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go` still has zero hits for `muse` (`git grep -in muse core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go` -> no output, re-run in this session) and a broader `git grep -in muse-spark core/pkg/capacity/` is also empty -- no muse model has ever had a pricing entry. Independently reconfirmed "no dollar cost is persisted anywhere" via a strict JSON-key scan of the transcript fixture (not a substring match): walked every key in every JSON object across `testdata/real-turn-completed.jsonl` and found zero keys containing `cost`/`price`/`usd`/`dollar` among 44 distinct keys total. This is expected/by-design (client-side pricing computation is the norm across every adapter) and is NOT part of this scenario's acceptance criteria (ModelName + ContextWindow only) -- unaffected by, and irrelevant to, this verdict.

## driver_capability -- gap:settings_model (RE-CONFIRMED against the current file, unchanged)

The task brief specifically calls out that the driver was separately touched by commit 0239a1bd for unrelated defects, so I re-read the CURRENT `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` rather than trusting the prior report:

- `SETTINGS_PATH="$4"` is still declared once, at line 83, with the comment "scenario settings blob; wire into the launch if the agent reads one" -- `grep -n SETTINGS_PATH replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` returns exactly this one hit, same as before.
- `launch_repl()` (lines 226-258) still hardcodes `tmux new-session -d -s "$SESSION" -x 200 -y 50 -c "${SES_CWD[$ACTIVE]}" "muse" --trust-workspace` (line 235) with no `--model` flag and no `$SETTINGS_PATH` read anywhere in the function. `--trust-workspace` itself IS new since the prior assessment -- commit 0239a1bd's defect #1 added it to close an unrelated bug (the untrusted-workspace modal eating the first prompt) -- but this is orthogonal to model selection; the function still launches whatever the account's DEFAULT model is.
- The step-dispatch loop's `keys)` arm (line 453) is still `not_implemented keys || break` -- unchanged. Live-confirmed in the prior assessment (not re-driven live this session, since neither fix commit touches the picker) that `/model <id>` sent as one line opens the SAME arrow-key picker as a bare `/model` and silently ignores the trailing argument, so `slash`/`send` cannot substitute for the missing `keys` step.
- `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean"` (line 139) is unchanged; the recipe's actual steps (send/wait_turn/sleep/exit_clean) are all covered, so recipe-lint passes clean -- the gap is specifically the LAUNCH-time model pin, not the scripted turn itself.

The fix is still the same, well-precedented port: mirror kiro-cli's `driver-interactive.sh` (lines ~88-111, 291), which reads `.model` from `$SETTINGS_PATH` and appends `--model $MODEL` to its launch command. `record` should port this before driving; until then, a recording of this cell would silently launch the account default instead of a genuine non-default pin.

## What changed since e055cef4 (explicit diff for the re-assessment)

- **daemon_capability: bug -> full.** Both stacked gaps closed by 609cb28d (parser.go's missing `.Total`, and a NEW ContextWindow fallback via catalog.go reading muse's own local model-catalog cache) -- independently re-verified via a fresh probe against the committed fixture, not taken from the commit message.
- **driver_capability: gap:settings_model -> gap:settings_model, unchanged.** Re-confirmed against the CURRENT driver-interactive.sh (post-0239a1bd): SETTINGS_PATH still unread by launch_repl, keys still a stub. 0239a1bd's five fixes (trust-workspace, step_send delay, resolve_transcript scope, exit_clean wiring, turn_count error surfacing) are all real but orthogonal to model selection.
- **New caveat introduced by the fix itself:** ContextWindow resolution now depends on a machine-local cache file muse lazily populates (not a transcript signal), which is a genuine environment precondition for a clean recording, not an event-flow question -- this did not exist as a consideration under the prior bug verdict since ContextWindow could not resolve via ANY path before.
- **Unchanged:** agent_supports=yes; cost_nonzero=false (still no muse pricing entry, still not part of this scenario's acceptance criteria); the vacuous-pass mitigation (asserting `observations.model` as an exact match on the pinned id, not merely non-unknown).
caveats: ContextWindow resolution is a LOCAL FILESYSTEM read (~/.local/share/muse/model-catalog/*.json via catalog.go's contextWindowForModel), not a transcript/events.jsonl signal -- muse itself lazily populates this cache, so it is a load-bearing environment precondition for recording this cell cleanly: if the recording machine's muse account has never resolved a given model's context limit before, ContextWindow legitimately reads unknown (ContextWindowUnknown=true, never a fabricated number -- pinned by catalog_test.go's TestContextWindowForModel_NoDirectory) even though the daemon mechanism itself is correct. record should confirm the cache is populated for the pinned model before recording, or trigger population with a prior launch.

The specific pinned model (muse-spark-1.2) has not been directly confirmed to have its own row in the live catalog cache -- only muse-spark-1.3 and muse-spark-1.3-contributor have been directly observed (catalog.go's doc comment and catalog_test.go's fixture both trace to the same single original observation). Plausible since the account's /model picker enumerates muse-spark-1.2 as selectable, but record must verify ContextWindow actually resolves for THIS model at record time rather than assuming it from this cell's fixture-based confirmation (which used the DEFAULT model, muse-spark-1.3-contributor).

Driver gap unchanged, re-confirmed against the current file post-0239a1bd: launch_repl (driver-interactive.sh:226-258) still hardcodes `muse --trust-workspace` with no --model flag; SETTINGS_PATH (line 83) is still declared but unread; keys (line 453) is still not_implemented. Recording this cell without porting the settings.model knob (kiro-cli's driver-interactive.sh:~88-111,291 pattern) silently launches the account default model instead of the pinned one.

Vacuous-pass mitigation, carried forward unchanged: observations.model asserts an EXACT match on "muse-spark-1.2" (the pinned id), not merely non-empty/non-unknown -- a driver that never wires the launch flag correctly FAILS this assertion (surfacing the still-open gap) instead of silently passing on the account default.

cost_nonzero is asserted false, not true -- core/pkg/capacity has no pricing entry for any muse-spark-* model (git grep -in muse core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go: zero hits, re-confirmed this session) and no dollar-cost field is ever persisted by muse (independently reconfirmed via a strict JSON-key scan of testdata/real-turn-completed.jsonl across all 44 distinct keys, not a substring match). Not part of this scenario's acceptance criteria (ModelName + ContextWindow only) and not a defect -- by design, same as every other adapter's client-side pricing.

--trust-workspace is required on every launch (every staging cwd is freshly created) -- this is now ALREADY wired into driver-interactive.sh's launch_repl by commit 0239a1bd (previously a caveat about future driver work; now a settled baseline, carried forward only as a factual note).

muse-spark-1.2 was chosen as the pin because it is a live-confirmed selectable option in this account's /model picker (muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.3-contributor [default], muse-spark-1.2, muse-spark-1.2-contributor) -- account/tier-scoped, unverified on a different account.

sources.note: ev.Tokens.Total is now set at line 439 (bd.Input+bd.Output+bd.CacheRead+bd.CacheCreation5m); applyModelIdentity centralizes ModelName + ContextWindow lookup and is called from parseModelCompleted at line 421.

contextWindowForModel (catalog.go:57-88) scans every *.json under ~/.local/share/muse/model-catalog/ for a matching model_id row, returning (0,false) on any failure to resolve with confidence (no directory, unparseable file, no match, zero context_limit) -- each of these negative paths is pinned by a dedicated catalog_test.go case.
